scope: Real hosted Windows native baseline investigation and source-only coordinator qualification; no configuration reached
diagnosis: All six native reports across three source-bound cohorts stopped at baseline before configuration invocation.
The refined diagnostics identify a selected Up adapter with absent IPv4 and IPv6 registry keys and zero per-interface DNS-client rows on both AMD64 and ARM64.
The shape probe marks this adapter hardware=true and physical=true, so physical-only filtering would retain it.
Other adapters on both runners expose one DNS-client row per family and readable registry keys.
No raw logs, registry values, adapter names/GUIDs, host paths or accounts were read.
sourceInference: Configure-DNS selects all Up non-tunnel adapters before testing DNS-client exposure, and then reads every selected adapter registry profile. On fresh state this would include the observed non-DNS adapter and refuse capture; the actual product apply was not invoked by these runs, so this is a static inference rather than an observed product apply failure.

limitations: The actual source-built controllers passed native target/source identity checks, but system apply was not invoked because independent baseline capture failed.
